claim: At the United Nations on September 27, 2024, hours after Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu addressed the General Assembly, Jordan's Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi said the Arab and Muslim states would collectively guarantee Israel's security in exchange for Palestinian statehood. Speaking as a member of the Arab-Islamic Ministerial Committee, which he described as "mandated by 57 Arab and Muslim countries," he said: "All of us are willing to guarantee the security of Israel in the context of Israel ending the occupation." He specified the terms as a peace in which Israel is "accepted, normalized with all Arab countries in the context of ending the occupation, withdrawing from Arab territory, allowing for the emergence of an independent, sovereign Palestinian state on the June 4, 1967 lines with East Jerusalem as its capital," and challenged Israel to state its own: "if he does not want the two-state solution, can you ask Israeli officials what is their end-game — other than just wars and wars and wars?" The offer is not new. It restates the Arab Peace Initiative adopted unanimously by the 22 Arab League states at the Beirut summit in March 2002, which offered to consider the Arab-Israeli conflict ended, sign peace agreements and establish normal relations with Israel, in return for full withdrawal to the June 4, 1967 lines including the Golan Heights and a just solution for refugees under UN General Assembly Resolution 194. The committee Safadi spoke for was created by the joint Arab-Islamic extraordinary summit held in Riyadh on November 11, 2023, convening the League of Arab States and the 57-member Organisation of Islamic Cooperation. Successive Israeli governments have not accepted the initiative; Netanyahu has publicly rejected a Palestinian state on those terms.

sources.label: The Times of Israel — "Jordanian FM: Arab world willing to guarantee Israel's security if Palestinian state established," Sept. 27, 2024.
sources.quote: All of us are willing to guarantee the security of Israel in the context of Israel ending the occupation

sources.label: Al Arabiya English — "Israel can live in peace with Arab states if Palestinian state established: Jordan FM," Sept. 30, 2024; the June 4, 1967 lines and the "wars and wars and wars" exchange.
Arab Peace Initiative, adopted at the 14th Arab Summit, Beirut, March 28, 2002 — full text as circulated to the European Parliament.
United Nations — Arab Peace Initiative as transmitted to the Security Council and General Assembly (Letter from Lebanon, Arab League summit).
Organisation of Islamic Cooperation — final communiqué of the Joint Arab-Islamic Extraordinary Summit, Riyadh, Nov. 11, 2023, which created the ministerial committee.

notes: Backstage. The reel is a straight clip of a real press conference with no added framing, so the editorial work here is context rather than correction: the offer is presented online as though it were new, and the load-bearing fact is that it is the 2002 Arab Peace Initiative restated by a committee created in 2023. Both primaries are cited so a reader can compare the terms directly. Safadi's words are quoted from Times of Israel and Al Arabiya rather than a UN transcript because the remarks were made at a press conference, not from the rostrum, and are not in the verbatim record. Worth upgrading: UN Web TV holds video of Safadi's UNGA-week press appearances, and the Jordanian foreign ministry posts transcripts. The final sentence is the one most likely to be read as taking a side, so it is confined to what is on the record — that the initiative has not been accepted and that Netanyahu has publicly rejected Palestinian statehood on those terms — with no characterization of motive on either side. The reel's own framing, that there is 'no partner for peace in Israel,' is Safadi's assertion and is not adopted. Group A on the statement and the documents; the competing narratives are Group B.
